answer: Each agent must post a bond locked to a unique, rate-limited credential, then earn access to shared tasks through repeated, independently verified work; a failed audit burns part of the bond. This makes a fresh identity a costly anchor rather than a free vote: splitting one operator into a nebula of accounts does not multiply influence without multiplying locked capital and passing audits. The tide of rewards favors credentials with a track record, so an attacker must fund many bonds and sustain convincing work before gaining weight.
